issues.legal_issue: Property owned by the Union is exempt from municipal property tax when the property was not liable or treated as liable to that tax immediately before the Constitution commenced.
material_facts: The land and godowns were owned by the Union, and the godowns were constructed after the Constitution commenced.
The property for which tax was demanded was not subject to property tax immediately before the Constitution commenced.
No parliamentary law authorising the disputed property tax was identified.
issues.conclusion: The municipal corporation could not levy property tax on the Union-owned property, which was exempt under Article 285(1).
issues.legal_principle: Article 285(1) exempts Union property from State and local taxation, subject to the qualification in Article 285(2). Article 285(2) preserves only a tax to which the property was liable or treated as liable immediately before the Constitution commenced, maintaining the pre-existing position rather than creating a general power to tax Union property. The Court relied on Union of India, owner of the Eastern Railway v. Commissioner of Sahibganj Municipality (1973) 1 SCC 676; Union of India v. City Municipal Council, Bellary (1979) 2 SCC 1; Corporation of Calcutta v. Governors of St. Thomas’ School, Calcutta, AIR 1949 FC 121; and the earlier Calcutta decisions interpreting the corresponding provision of the Government of India Act, 1935.

rule.if: municipal_property_tax_appeal and union_owned_property and property_built_after_constitution and property_not_taxed_before_constitution and no_law_authorizes_property_tax

predicates.municipal_property_tax_appeal: The proceeding challenges a municipal demand for property tax on property.
predicates.union_owned_property: The property on which tax is demanded is owned by the Union.
predicates.property_built_after_constitution: The property for which tax is demanded came into existence after the Constitution commenced.
predicates.property_not_taxed_before_constitution: The property was not liable or treated as liable to the relevant property tax immediately before the Constitution commenced.
predicates.no_law_authorizes_property_tax: No law authorising the disputed property tax on the Union property applies.

issues.definition: When a municipal property-tax appeal concerns Union-owned property that came into existence after the Constitution commenced, was not then liable to the tax, and is not made taxable by law, the property is exempt from property tax.

issues.legal_issue: A municipality cannot impose property tax on an occupier of Union-owned property when doing so would defeat the constitutional exemption applicable to the property.
material_facts: The Union owned the land and godowns, while the appellant occupied and used the godowns for storage of food grains.
The appellant occupied the property on behalf of the Union and was not shown to be a lessee paying rent.
The property was exempt from property tax under Article 285(1).
The municipal corporation relied on the statutory rule assigning primary responsibility for property taxes to certain occupiers.
issues.conclusion: The occupier was not liable for property tax under the municipal statute because applying that provision to charge the occupier would defeat the constitutional exemption for the Union-owned property.
issues.legal_principle: Article 285(1) protects Union property from local property tax, and the municipal statute governing primary responsibility for property taxes must be construed consistently with that constitutional protection. The provision assigning responsibility to an occupier cannot be used to make the exemption ineffective. The Court distinguished Food Corporation of India v. Municipal Committee, Jalalabad (1999) 6 SCC 74 and Electronics Corporation of India Ltd. v. Secretary, Revenue Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh (1999) 4 SCC 458, which concerned property belonging to separate legal entities rather than Union-owned property.

rule.if: municipal_property_tax_appeal and union_owned_property and property_tax_exemption_applies and occupier_holds_directly_from_government and occupier_uses_property_for_government

predicates.municipal_property_tax_appeal: The proceeding challenges a municipal demand for property tax on property.
predicates.union_owned_property: The property on which tax is demanded is owned by the Union.
predicates.property_tax_exemption_applies: The property is constitutionally exempt from the disputed property tax.
predicates.occupier_holds_directly_from_government: The occupier holds the property immediately from the government.
predicates.occupier_uses_property_for_government: The occupier uses the property on behalf of the government.

issues.definition: When an occupier holds Union-owned property directly from the government and uses it on the government's behalf, the occupier is not liable for property tax if the property itself is exempt.

issues.legal_issue: Constitutional exemption of Union property from property tax does not exempt an occupier from charges that are fees for services actually provided.
material_facts: The municipal corporation provided services, including water-related services, in connection with the property.
The appellant accepted that it was liable to pay charges for services rendered by the municipal corporation.
The appellant was exempt from property tax because the property belonged to the Union.
issues.conclusion: The appellant remained liable for charges for services rendered, and the municipal corporation could conduct an enquiry under the applicable municipal procedure to determine the relevant rateable value.
issues.legal_principle: Article 285 exempts Union property from taxation but does not bar fees for services actually rendered. The substance of the charge, rather than its label, determines whether it is a tax or a service fee. The Court relied on Union of India v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2007) 11 SCC 324, which distinguished property taxes from charges for water supply and sewerage services, and noted the municipal enquiry procedure under Section 144 of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act, 1888.

rule.if: municipal_charge_dispute and union_owned_property and services_actually_rendered and charge_is_for_those_services

predicates.municipal_charge_dispute: The proceeding concerns municipal charges associated with property owned by the Union.
predicates.union_owned_property: The property associated with the charges is owned by the Union.
predicates.services_actually_rendered: The municipal corporation actually provided services in connection with the property.
predicates.charge_is_for_those_services: The charge compensates for the services provided rather than taxing the property.

issues.definition: When a municipal corporation actually provides services in connection with Union-owned property and the charge is for those services, the service charge remains payable.
